01 / Lab Research

Movement, Attention & Assessment

Research AssistantUNC Wilmington · Dr. Len Lecci

Spring 2026 – Present

Spring 2026

The Study & My Role

How does ADHD assessment performance differ from deliberately simulated symptoms?

I ran and scored standardized assessments with participants with ADHD, healthy controls, and people asked to simulate symptoms. We compared assessment performance and survey responses across the groups.

My Assessment Contributions
  • Participant Coordination

    Managed appointments, lab preparation, screening, and study procedures as part of the research assistant team.

  • Consent & Participant Care

    Explained study requirements, voluntary participation, and confidentiality during informed consent and debriefing.

  • Standardized Assessment

    Administered memory, attention, working-memory, and gait assessments, along with standardized scales measuring generalized anxiety and depressive symptoms, under established protocols.

  • Data Quality

    Scored behavioral assessments and entered study data in REDCap.

Methods & Tools

REDCap; SportGait gait assessment; TOMM2; CAARS-2; Digit Span; CES-D; BAI; and standardized interviewing scripts.

Research from Dr. Lecci’s lab on detecting invalid assessment performance.

TOMM 2 Reaction Times: mTBI & Simulated Symptoms ↗

Research Article Review & Presentation

We each review a research article related to our study and present it to the lab team. In spring 2026, I reviewed a published study of how ADHD symptoms vary with age and biological sex.

02 / Collaborative Study

AI Permission, Performance & Confidence

Collaborative Research StudyThree-person research team

Four-week summer class

The Study & My Role

Our three-person team studied whether explicitly permitting AI use on assignments affects students’ problem-solving performance and confidence. We completed the study during a four-week summer class.

Survey Design & Statistical Analysis

I built the Qualtrics survey, helped design the experiment, and cleaned and analyzed the data in Jamovi.

  • Survey Engineering

    Built screening branches, balanced random assignment, timed responses, and custom validation with fallback logic in Qualtrics.

  • Experimental Structure

    Implemented AI permission conditions alongside self-reported gender and disclosures of outside assistance.

  • Timed Tasks

    Configured 90-second response windows for four CRT-2 cognitive reflection items.

  • Analysis

    Used descriptive statistics and a two-way between-subjects ANOVA in Jamovi to evaluate main and interaction effects.
